title: Average Lies
subtitle: When the mean misleads and the median reveals the truth
conceptSummary: Mean (average) is pulled by outliers. Median (middle value) is more robust. Always check both!

dialogue.text: Welcome to Insight City! Here we turn data into understanding. The fraud report claims 'average transaction is ₹6,800'. But something feels off.
One massive transaction from the mastermind is skewing the average. Find the REAL typical transaction using median thinking.

teachMoment.title: Mean vs Median
teachMoment.body:
Example salaries: ₹20k, ₹22k, ₹25k, ₹28k, ₹200k
Mean: (20+22+25+28+200)/5 = ₹59k — misleading!
Median: ₹25k (middle value) — more realistic

When data has outliers (extremely high or low values), the median is more honest.

Rule of thumb:
• Symmetric data → Mean is fine
• Skewed data / outliers → Use Median

task.instruction: Look at the bad chart shown. It shows the MEAN transaction amount. Choose the correct fix that better represents the 'typical' transaction.

badChart.title: Typical Transaction Amount
badChart.problem: Mean is skewed by 2 large fraudulent transactions (28999, 22999). Most transactions are under 5000.

options.label: Show both Mean and Median
options.explanation: Showing both gives the full picture. Median (~3500) reveals the typical customer, while mean shows the overall total impact.

options.label: Use a bigger bar chart
options.explanation: Making the chart bigger doesn't fix the misleading metric.

options.label: Remove the outlier transactions from the data
options.explanation: Removing data hides important information. The outliers are the fraud we're investigating!

options.label: Switch to a pie chart
options.explanation: A pie chart doesn't help here and would still use mean.

hints.text: The problem is the mean is pulled high by large outliers. What better represents 'typical'?
Median = the middle value when sorted. It's not affected by extremes. Show BOTH mean and median.
The correct fix is 'Show both Mean and Median' — it gives the full picture without hiding data.

winDialogue.text: The median transaction is ₹3,499 — totally normal. The mean of ₹6,821 was inflated by just 2 fraudulent mega-transactions.
Good. Now choose the right chart to show the fraud's geographic spread. A bar chart? Map? Scatter plot? Case 2 decides.

storyBeat: Statistics don't lie, but they can mislead. The fraud's financial footprint was hidden behind a deceptive average. With the right metrics, the truth emerges. One final chart to make the case airtight.
